parameters.content:
## A · AI4SG Overview
Click **Execute workflow**: the **run page** opens. Choose the domain, countries, languages, source types and how many sources to analyse in depth, then **Start run**. The same run page is always at /form/ai4sg-run (locally http://localhost:5678/form/ai4sg-run).
**Every candidate the search finds is kept** (nothing is cut): each is downloaded into the source library, screened cheaply, and the best ones are analysed in depth, **new projects first**. Screened sources that do not fit this run's budget wait as *queued* and are analysed first in the next run of the same domain. Each run's numbers (found, new, screened, analysed, queued) are in the `runs` table and on the audit page: http://localhost:5678/webhook/ai4sg-audit

### ⚙️ Run page = this run's settings
- Domain: all, or one domain module
- Countries (+ other countries)
- Search languages: local / English
- Source types
- Topic focus, published from (year)
- Search engine: Codex agent / single API call
- Max web searches
- Results per search (a target, not a cap)
- Max sources to analyse in depth
- Relevance screen: broad / balanced / strict

Chosen each time; the skill files are not edited for a run.

### 🧑‍🔬 Expert deliverables = the interface
`skills/search/SKILL.md`: what counts as AI for Social Good; how to search each source type; the fixed academic databases; local-language keywords; each country's ISO code and local languages.  → used by **B · Search** (and by the screen in C1)
`skills/extraction/SKILL.md` + `skills/extraction/examples/`: the fields to extract, how to interpret them, and the experts' worked extractions.  → **C2 · Extract**
`skills/domains/<domain>.md`: the domain chosen on the run page: scope, search terms, academic databases, 4 domain fields, outcome categories.  → added to both skills

### After the search: four stages in a straight line
Each stage is its own sub-workflow; the next starts only when the previous has finished (even if it had nothing to do).
**① Collect & Screen**: download this run's new sources (and earlier failed downloads) into the source library, then screen each one with GPT-6 Luna. Passed sources join the queue.
**② Organise & Extract**: GPT-6 Sol organises the domain's whole queue in one call: each source into a deployment (project P-…) under its tool (T-…), duplicates marked, known deployments that are the same merged, and (with *Max sources to analyse*) the sources most worth analysing chosen. C2 then analyses the chosen sources (all, without a budget): extraction with the deployment as context, quote check.
**③ Project Summaries**: re-summarise the deployments that got new sources (C3).
**④ Finish Run**: count what happened and store it in `runs`.
Sources not analysed are listed on the audit page (*Not analysed yet*), where a reviewer can send them to the analysis.

parameters.formDescription: Choose what to search in this run. Each web search covers one country × language × source type (e.g. Bangladesh × Bengali × News). Every source found is kept; sources collected in earlier runs are skipped. Choosing a domain applies that domain's rules: what counts, where to search, the fields and outcomes to extract. These rules, local keywords and extraction rules stay in the experts' skill files. Results: audit page

parameters.query:
-- keep every candidate not seen before (same URL or same DOI as an earlier source = already known)
WITH cand AS (
  SELECT r.*, o.ord
  FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) WITH ORDINALITY AS o(j, ord),
       jsonb_to_record(o.j) AS r(url text, url_norm text, title text, title_en text, source_type text, format text, search_engine text,
                                 country text, language text, why_relevant text, domain text, doi text, database text,
                                 found_via_url text, relation text, project_name text, files jsonb, title_norm text)
)
INSERT INTO sources (url, url_norm, title, title_en, source_type, format, country, language, why_relevant, search_engine, domain,
                     run_id, status, doi, database, found_via_url, relation, project_guess, files)
SELECT url, url_norm, title, title_en, source_type, format, country, language, why_relevant, search_engine, NULLIF(domain, ''),
       $2::bigint, 'candidate', NULLIF(lower(doi), ''), NULLIF(database, ''), NULLIF(found_via_url, ''), NULLIF(relation, ''),
       NULLIF(project_name, ''), COALESCE(files, '[]'::jsonb)
FROM cand c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sources s WHERE s.url_norm = c.url_norm)
  AND (COALESCE(c.doi, '') = '' OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sources s WHERE lower(s.doi) = lower(c.doi)))
  -- the same title as a source already in the database (another version of a known paper)
  AND (length(COALESCE(c.title_norm, '')) <= 25 OR NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM sources s WHERE trim(regexp_replace(lower(s.title), '[^[:alnum:]]+', ' ', 'g')) = c.title_norm))
ORDER BY ord
ON CONFLICT (url_norm) DO NOTHING
RETURNING id AS source_id, url, doi, format, country, language, files

-- link cascaded sources to the source that led to them, then store the search numbers
WITH linked AS (
  UPDATE sources c SET found_via = p.id
  FROM sources p
  WHERE c.run_id = $1 AND c.found_via IS NULL AND c.found_via_url IS NOT NULL AND p.id <> c.id
    AND (p.url = c.found_via_url OR p.url_norm = lower(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(c.found_via_url, '#.*$', ''), '/$', '')))
  RETURNING c.id
)
UPDATE runs SET counts = counts || jsonb_build_object('found', $2::int, 'unique', $3::int, 'new', $4::int, 'versions_merged', $5::int,
                                                      'already_known', $3::int - $4::int, 'cascade_linked', (SELECT count(*) FROM linked))
WHERE id = $1 RETURNING id AS run_id

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Start Run').first().json.run_id, $('Prepare Candidates').first().json.found, $('Prepare Candidates').first().json.unique, $('Save Candidates').all().filter(i => i.json.source_id).length, $('Prepare Candidates').first().json.versions_merged || 0 ] }}

parameters.query:
WITH r AS (SELECT id, started_at, domain FROM runs WHERE id = $1),
     mine AS (SELECT s.* FROM sources s, r WHERE s.run_id = r.id),
     analysed AS (SELECT e.source_id, s.run_id FROM extractions e JOIN sources s ON s.id = e.source_id, r WHERE e.created_at >= r.started_at)
UPDATE runs SET finished_at = now(), counts = counts || jsonb_build_object(
  'cascaded',        (SELECT count(*) FROM mine WHERE found_via_url IS NOT NULL),
  'downloaded',      (SELECT count(*) FROM mine WHERE status <> 'candidate' AND status <> 'collect_failed'),
  'download_failed', (SELECT count(*) FROM mine WHERE status = 'collect_failed'),
  'full_text',       (SELECT count(*) FROM mine WHERE text_level = 'full'),
  'abstract_only',   (SELECT count(*) FROM mine WHERE text_level = 'abstract'),
  'retried',         (SELECT count(*) FROM sources s, r WHERE s.run_id IS DISTINCT FROM r.id AND s.collected_at >= r.started_at),
  'retried_ok',      (SELECT count(*) FROM sources s, r WHERE s.run_id IS DISTINCT FROM r.id AND s.collected_at >= r.started_at
                        AND s.text_level IN ('full', 'abstract')),
  'screened',        (SELECT count(*) FROM mine WHERE screen IS NOT NULL),
  'passed_screen',   (SELECT count(*) FROM mine WHERE status IN ('passed', 'extracted')),
  'filtered_out',    (SELECT count(*) FROM mine WHERE status = 'filtered_out'),
  'analysed',        (SELECT count(*) FROM analysed),
  'analysed_from_queue', (SELECT count(*) FROM analysed WHERE analysed.run_id IS DISTINCT FROM $1),
  'queued',          (SELECT count(*) FROM sources s, r WHERE s.status = 'passed' AND s.domain IS NOT DISTINCT FROM r.domain),
  'new_projects',    (SELECT count(*) FROM ai_projects p, r WHERE p.created_at >= r.started_at),
  'new_tools',       (SELECT count(*) FROM ai_tools t, r WHERE t.created_at >= r.started_at),
  'duplicates',      (SELECT count(*) FROM sources s WHERE s.status = 'duplicate' AND s.pick->>'run_id' = $1::text),
  'organised_by',    (SELECT s.pick->>'method' FROM sources s WHERE s.pick->>'run_id' = $1::text LIMIT 1),
  'projects_updated', (SELECT count(*) FROM ai_projects p, r WHERE p.updated_at >= r.started_at))
WHERE id = $1 RETURNING id AS run_id, counts

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ status: 'done', execution_id: $execution.id, result: { run_id: $json.run_id, counts: $json.counts } }) }}
